records.title: The Independent Living Donor Advocate: An Essential Role for Living Kidney Donation.
records.population_setting: US living kidney donor transplant programs (post-2007 CMS/UNOS regulation)
records.key_finding: Post-2007 US regulation requires transplant programs to appoint an independent living donor advocate or advocate team, structurally separate from the recipient's care team, specifically to avoid any perception of conflict of interest between donor and recipient.
records.relevance_to_tphe: analogy (non-domain-matched) to R4 no-stake assessor: transplant-medicine analogy — regulator-mandated separation of the person assessing/protecting the vulnerable party from the team with a stake in the transaction proceeding.

records.title: The Psychosocial and Independent Living Donor Advocate Evaluation and Post-surgery Care of Living Donors.
records.journal: Journal of Clinical Psychology in Medical Settings
records.population_setting: US live organ donor transplant programs
records.key_finding: Describes CMS/UNOS-mandated independent donor advocate evaluation process, separated from the transplant candidate's team, covering informed consent, psychosocial evaluation and voluntariness of donation.
records.relevance_to_tphe: analogy (non-domain-matched) to R4 no-stake assessor: transplant-medicine analogy — shows a regulated, standardized process for keeping evaluation of a vulnerable party's welfare separate from the professionals who benefit from the procedure occurring.

records.title: Ethical Analysis and Policy Recommendations Regarding Domino Liver Transplantation.
records.population_setting: Domino liver donor transplant candidates (pediatric case example)
records.key_finding: Proposes a 'Domino Donor Advocate', modeled explicitly on the independent living donor advocate, plus two consent processes separated in time, to protect voluntariness when the same party stands to gain from securing consent.
records.relevance_to_tphe: analogy (non-domain-matched) to R4 no-stake assessor and P5 referral timing (separated processes before the day): transplant-medicine analogy — reinforces that a party with a stake in an irreversible transaction should not be the one certifying voluntariness/safety.

records.title: Ethics and the facial plastic surgeon.
records.population_setting: Facial plastic/cosmetic surgery practice
records.key_finding: Identifies an inherent conflict of interest when the clinician who evaluates whether a patient should proceed to an elective procedure is the same person who financially benefits from the patient proceeding; discusses informed consent, beneficence/non-maleficence and justice as safeguards.
records.relevance_to_tphe: analogy (non-domain-matched) to R4 no-stake assessor: unrelated-field ethics analogy — names the mechanism T-PHE is designed against, an evaluator with financial gain contingent on the client proceeding, in an unrelated clinical field.

records.title: Dual relationships in psychotherapy.
records.population_setting: Psychotherapy practice, US licensing-board context
records.key_finding: Reviews concurrent and sequential dual relationships between therapist and patient; combining roles such as evaluator and service-provider as a subtype is the search-author's own inference, not a phrase used in the abstract itself, which the abstract's professional-ethics attention to role combinations does not explicitly name.
records.relevance_to_tphe: analogy (non-domain-matched) to R4 no-stake assessor: unrelated-field (psychotherapy) ethics analogy — foundational dual-relationship ethics literature; the educator-as-vendor combination in T-PHE is offered as a structurally similar dual-relationship configuration, independent of intent.

records.title: Dual relationships in mental health practice: issues for clinicians in rural settings.
records.journal: Australian and New Zealand Journal of Psychiatry
records.population_setting: Rural mental health practice, multiple professions (psychiatry, psychology, OT, social work, nursing)
records.key_finding: Finds professional ethical codes provide little concrete guidance on non-sexual dual relationships despite their being common in small/rural settings; empirical research on their harms/benefits is limited.
records.relevance_to_tphe: complicates R4: shows the field itself lacks strong empirical/guidance consensus on dual roles, so T-PHE's no-stake-assessor rule is a precautionary design choice rather than one backed by outcome trials — should be stated honestly as such.

records.title: The average predictive validity of intimate partner violence risk assessment instruments.
records.population_setting: Five IPV risk-assessment instruments (ODARA, SARA, DA, DVSI, K-SID) across multiple validation studies
records.key_finding: ODARA had highest weighted AUC=.666 (k=5), then SARA AUC=.628, DA AUC=.618, DVSI AUC=.582, K-SID AUC=.537; only 9/20 (45%) of predictive-validity estimates involved the instrument administered correctly per its intended protocol.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (b): shows predictive validity depends materially on who/how administers the tool — under half of estimates used correct administration — directly relevant to specifying WHO (a no-stake trained assessor) administers a P5 risk screen, not just which tool.

records.title: Assessing the Danger: Validation of Taiwan Intimate Partner Violence Danger Assessment.
records.population_setting: 543 female IPV victims in a Taiwanese victim-services program
records.key_finding: TIPVDA showed strong discriminant power and ROC-AUC support for predicting lethal-danger risk, with stronger predictive power at the high-dangerousness end.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (b): a structured, validated IPV danger-assessment tool administered by front-line victim-services professionals (not by an interested party) is what underlies a credible risk screen model for P5/R4.

records.title: Validation and adaptation of the danger assessment-5: A brief intimate partner violence risk assessment.
records.population_setting: 1,081 women recruited by police at domestic-violence scenes 2009-2013; 619 (57.3%) re-interviewed ~7 months later
records.key_finding: DA-5 AUC=.68 for predicting severe/near-lethal re-assault; adding a strangulation item did not significantly change accuracy; authors recommend immediate referral protocols for high-risk survivors identified by the brief tool.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (b): a short, healthcare-settings-appropriate IPV risk tool (DA-5) with documented predictive validity and an explicit referral pathway is a workable model for a brief, non-stakeholder-administered safety check.

records.title: Accounting for Multiple Nonfatal Strangulation in Intimate Partner Violence Risk Assessment.
records.population_setting: Independent validation sample, n=389, IPV survivors
records.key_finding: Updated Danger Assessment predicted near-fatal violence at 7-8 month follow-up significantly better than the original; the DA and DA-I are intended to be used as a collaboration between IPV survivors and advocates as tools for education and intervention.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (b) and R4: reiterates that DA-family tools are designed to be used with an advocate role, reinforcing why an independent assessor (not the service provider) is the appropriate administrator.

records.title: [The Ontario Domestic Assault Risk Assessment (ODARA) - Validity und authorised German translation of an intimate partner violence screening tool].
records.population_setting: IPV cases assessed by police, hospital and victim-services staff (multi-professional)
records.key_finding: ODARA was designed to be brief and scorable by a wide range of practitioners (police, hospital, victim services) using easily collectable information, to reliably discriminate low- from high-risk cases and guide intervention.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (b): explicitly documents ODARA's design intent to be administered by trained third-party practitioners across settings, not by an interested party — a template for who should run a P5 check.

records.title: Unpacking Multiagency Structured Professional Judgment Risk Assessments for Family Violence.
records.population_setting: Multiagency family-violence triage teams (Integrated Safety Response), New Zealand
records.key_finding: It was often unclear which recorded factors actually drove the team's risk category, and whether those factors were empirically validated predictors, raising questions about the transparency/reliability of multiagency structured-judgment risk categorization.
records.relevance_to_tphe: complicates (b)/R4: even independent, multiagency (non-stakeholder) risk assessment teams can produce risk ratings whose basis is opaque — independence of the assessor does not by itself guarantee a valid or transparent risk judgment; T-PHE's assessor role needs documented criteria, not just no-stake status.

records.title: Assessment and management of risk for intimate partner violence by police officers using the Spousal Assault Risk Assessment Guide.
records.population_setting: Police officers using SARA in Sweden
records.key_finding: SARA assessments had significant predictive validity for police risk-management recommendations and recidivism; higher intervention levels reduced recidivism in high-risk cases but increased it in low-risk cases (mediation effect).
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (b): demonstrates a structured professional-judgment IPV tool administered by an institutionally separate party (police, not a relationship-interested actor) with documented outcome effects — a workable independence template, while also showing risk-tiered response matters, not one-size-fits-all referral.

records.title: Investigating racial disparities in violence risk assessment using the Spousal Assault Risk Assessment Guide-Version 3.
records.population_setting: Individuals with IPV histories assessed via SARA-V3, Canada (Indigenous vs non-Indigenous)
records.key_finding: Structured-professional-judgment risk ratings (not only actuarial tools) showed racial disparities between Indigenous and non-Indigenous participants in risk factors and summary ratings.
records.relevance_to_tphe: complicates R4/P5: independence from financial stake does not eliminate other assessor biases (e.g., demographic/cultural); a no-stake-assessor design still needs bias-awareness safeguards, especially for a Thai premarital context with its own social/religious stratification.

records.title: "Increasing Warm Handoffs: Optimizing Community Based Referrals in Primary Care Using QI Methodology.
records.journal: Journal of Primary Care & Community Health
records.population_setting: Pediatric primary care clinic, Community Health Worker (CHW) referrals for unmet social needs
records.key_finding: QI methods doubled the rate of successful warm handoffs between clinic staff and CHWs for families with unmet social needs (reported as a two-fold increase over the intervention period).
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (c): demonstrates 'warm handoff' as a distinct, measurable process step (not just a screening checkbox) that materially changes whether at-risk people actually reach the next service — supports framing the check-in as a gateway that must connect to a real handoff, not an endpoint.

records.title: Evaluating a social risk screening and referral program in an urban safety-net hospital emergency department.
records.journal: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians Open
records.population_setting: Adult ED patients, urban safety-net hospital, Sept 2020-Dec 2021
records.key_finding: 58.5% of eligible patients were screened; of interviewed screen-positive patients, only 24.5% recalled receiving a resource guide, and staff-observed discharge interactions rarely discussed guides (2/13); staff themselves preferred warm handoff over passive resource guides.
records.relevance_to_tphe: contradicts/complicates a naive check-in model: shows a significant gap between screening (check-in) and actual connection to help — a check-in alone, without an enforced warm-handoff mechanism, frequently fails to translate into support reaching the person, directly relevant to defining T-PHE's failure criterion for the check-in.

records.title: Efficacy of a short message service brief contact intervention (SMS-SOS) in reducing repetition of hospital-treated self-harm.
records.population_setting: Three hospitals, Sydney, Australia, 2017-2019; self-harm presentations
records.key_finding: Repetition event rate lower with SMS brief-contact vs treatment-as-usual: IRR=0.79 (6mo), 0.78 (12mo, 95% CI 0.64-0.95), 0.78 (24mo, 95% CI 0.66-0.91) — a 22% reduction; but no significant difference in time to first repeat event (HR=0.96, 95% CI 0.72-1.26).
records.relevance_to_tphe: analogy (non-domain-matched) to (c): a suicide/self-harm brief-contact trial — an inexpensive brief-contact 'check-in' model can produce a modest, statistically supported reduction in repeat harm, but did not delay the first repeat event — offered as convergent analogy for what a check-in model can honestly claim, not as evidence T-PHE's own check-in is effective.

records.title: Comparative effectiveness of safety planning intervention with instrumental support calls (ISC) versus caring contacts (CC) two-way text messages: the SPARC Trial protocol.
records.population_setting: 720 adolescents (12-17y) and 790 adults screening positive for suicide risk in ED/primary care, US
records.key_finding: Protocol only (no outcome data yet reported in this record); establishes that two brief follow-up/'check-in' contact models (instrumental support calls vs caring-contact texts) are being head-to-head compared for suicide-risk follow-up.
records.relevance_to_tphe: analogy (non-domain-matched), design template only: a suicide-risk brief-contact trial protocol — shows brief-contact/check-in models are an active, rigorously tested category of intervention; caution — this record reports trial design, not results, so it cannot itself be cited for effect size.

records.title: Comparative effectiveness of two versions of a caring contacts intervention in healthcare providers, staff and patients.
records.population_setting: Primary care patients and healthcare providers/staff reporting adverse mental health outcomes, Jan-Jul 2021, 6-month follow-up
records.key_finding: Compared Caring Contacts with vs without an introductory phone call; tested whether check-ins from an unknown sender are as effective as from someone the recipient met. There were no significant differences in loneliness at 6 months by treatment arm in either stratum; including an initial phone call added operational complexity without significantly improving the effectiveness of the Caring Contacts program.
records.relevance_to_tphe: analogy (non-domain-matched) to (c): a suicide-prevention-adjacent (Caring Contacts) trial — tests whether the identity/relationship of the check-in sender matters for effectiveness, but found no significant difference between conditions; offered as a null-result caution, not as evidence T-PHE's check-in delivery mode affects outcomes.

records.title: Interventions for attempted suicide.
records.population_setting: People with a history of suicide attempt, multiple settings
records.key_finding: Among reviewed approaches (pharmacological, psychosocial, brief active contact/outreach, digital), brief-contact and follow-up interventions showed the most robust effects on reducing repeat suicidal behaviour, especially valuable in emergency settings due to their brevity.
records.relevance_to_tphe: analogy (non-domain-matched) to (c): a suicide/self-harm brief-contact narrative synthesis — corroborates that brief-contact/check-in-style interventions are among the better-evidenced prevention approaches in that domain, offered as convergent analogy, not as evidence T-PHE's own check-in is effective.

records.title: Care utilization and clinical outcomes among high-risk patients enrolled in a postpartum navigation program: a retrospective matched cohort study.
records.population_setting: Pregnant patients >32 weeks at risk for postpartum morbidity, Oct 2023-Sept 2024
records.key_finding: Navigator conducted check-ins at delivery, 2, 6 and 12 weeks; 80.7% attended the 2-week check-in but only 48.4% completed the full program; navigation was associated with improved hypertension monitoring, breastfeeding duration and mental-health screening versus a matched historical cohort.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports (c) with a fidelity caveat: shows a scheduled check-in/touchpoint model produces measurable clinical benefit even though under half completed the full program — evidence that partial check-in engagement can still yield benefit, but completion/attrition (48.4%) is a realistic ceiling to expect, relevant to defining T-PHE's own completion-based failure criterion.

records.title: Implementation Fidelity and Theory-Informed Dose Effects of a Teen Pregnancy Prevention Program for Native American Youth.
records.design: Process/fidelity evaluation nested in RCT arm (N=266)
records.population_setting: Native youth aged 11-19 and a trusted adult, Respecting the Circle of Life (RCL) program
records.key_finding: High fidelity/quality (4.40-4.82/5) and 96.6% of planned activities completed; average dosage 7/9 lessons; no significant association found between theoretical-construct dosage and outcomes.
records.relevance_to_tphe: complicates (d): even with high measured fidelity and dosage, dosage was not associated with outcomes — a caution against assuming that a programme judged 'complete/high-fidelity' by process metrics is thereby judged effective; fidelity and outcome are separable axes T-PHE should not conflate in its own completion criterion.
records.evidence_level: Process/fidelity evaluation (single-hop empirical, null dose-outcome finding)

records.title: Adapting the Diabetes Prevention Program for low- and middle-income countries: preliminary implementation findings from lifestyle Africa.
records.population_setting: Overweight/obese adults in chronic-disease support groups, urban South Africa, delivered by community health workers
records.key_finding: 10/11 groups completed all 17 core sessions; average attendance 54%; only 35% attended ≥75% of sessions; fidelity monitoring found 84% of required procedures completed.
records.relevance_to_tphe: complicates (d): shows attendance/completion metrics (54% average, 35% at ≥75%) can be modest even in a well-monitored, community-health-worker-delivered prevention programme — realistic benchmark against which a wedding-vendor-delivered T-PHE classroom's own completion numbers should be judged, and a reminder that low completion is common even without provider incentive distortion.

records.title: Comparison of recidivism rates for a teenage trauma prevention program after the addition of high-fidelity patient simulation.
records.population_setting: Court-ordered teen trauma-prevention program participants, US
records.key_finding: Adding high-fidelity simulation to the program did not significantly change recidivism rates versus historical controls (55% recidivism within 6 years; 8.4% at 6 months rising to ~20% at 1 year); participants reported positive attitude change (e.g., 30% would decrease speed) despite no behavioural/recidivism effect.
records.relevance_to_tphe: contradicts a naive 'more program content = better outcome' assumption, and supports (d)'s caution: increasing programme fidelity/intensity (adding simulation) produced favourable self-reported attitudes but no measurable reduction in the actual outcome (recidivism) — directly parallels the risk that a well-delivered T-PHE classroom check-in produces reported satisfaction without changing the outcome that matters (safety).
records.evidence_level: Historical-control comparison study (single-hop empirical, null outcome finding)

gaps_noted: No PubMed-indexed literature was found that directly studies 'conflict of interest of a wedding-service provider acting as premarital-education assessor' — this exact configuration does not appear to be a studied topic; evidence is necessarily analogical (organ-donor advocacy, clinical dual-relationship ethics, facial-plastic-surgery COI) rather than domain-matched.

Direct queries for 'independent assessor' + safeguarding/risk-assessment and for 'who administers' + IPV screening returned zero or off-topic hits; independence-of-assessor as an explicit IPV-screening design variable is under-studied in PubMed-indexed literature (much of this literature lives in grey/policy sources, e.g. SafeLives DASH guidance, not indexed in PubMed).

No Thailand-specific or premarital-education-specific record was found for this angle; angle (a)-(d) evidence is drawn from adjacent fields (organ transplantation ethics, IPV risk assessment, suicide/self-harm brief-contact trials, US pediatric/prevention-science implementation studies) and must be explicitly flagged as analogical transfer, not direct T-PHE evidence, in any manuscript use.

Fidelity/incentive angle (d) surfaced good evidence that fidelity and outcome can be decoupled (RCL, teen trauma simulation), but no record specifically studied programmes 'judged by completion' as an incentive-distorting metric in a provider-owns-downstream-business context — this specific incentive structure (educator paid on completion/booking) remains unstudied in the retrieved set.
limits_of_this_search: Search restricted to PubMed-indexed records only, retrieved via NCBI E-utilities esearch/efetch with title/abstract field queries; grey literature (SafeLives DASH toolkit documentation, UK/Thai safeguarding board guidance, WHO LIVES/IPV clinical handbooks) that likely bears directly on assessor-independence and check-in models is NOT indexed in PubMed and was therefore excluded by design, even though it may be more directly relevant than several included analogical records. All key numeric findings were read from PubMed abstracts (efetch) only; no full-text verification was performed. No record found asserts or implies that T-PHE itself is effective; all records are used strictly to position/complicate/support isolated design components (assessor independence, check-in framing, fidelity-outcome decoupling).
